title: What is recorded before a suicide
context: In Colorado, more than half of the people who died by suicide had a recorded mental health problem, but fewer than a third were in treatment when they died.
ask: What did investigators record, and what could they not see?
unit: Share of suicides with known circumstances (toxicology: of those tested)

rows.label: A current mental health problem
rows.about: Investigators found a mental health condition diagnosed by a professional, current at the time of death.

rows.label: Diagnosed depression
rows.about: A current diagnosis of depression or dysthymia was recorded.

rows.label: Current depressed mood
rows.about: Family, friends or records described the person as depressed or down at the time, whether or not a diagnosis existed.

rows.label: Diagnosed anxiety
rows.about: A current diagnosis of an anxiety disorder was recorded.

rows.label: Diagnosed bipolar disorder
rows.about: A current diagnosis of bipolar disorder was recorded.

rows.label: Diagnosed schizophrenia
rows.about: A current diagnosis of schizophrenia was recorded.

rows.label: Diagnosed ADHD
rows.about: A current diagnosis of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder was recorded.

rows.label: Ever treated for mental health or substance use
rows.about: Any record of treatment at any time: counselling, medication or a programme.

rows.label: In treatment at the time
rows.about: The person was receiving mental health or substance use treatment when they died.

rows.label: Antidepressant found at death
rows.about: An antidepressant was found in the toxicology tests after death. It shows the drug was taken, not why or whether it was prescribed to that person.

rows.label: Amphetamine found at death (prescribed or not)
rows.about: An amphetamine was found in toxicology. The test does not separate a prescribed ADHD medicine from illicit methamphetamine.

place: Colorado residents, 2018–2022 (6,220 suicides with known circumstances)

source.publisher: Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment
source.title: HealthWatch No. 128: Suicide in Colorado, 2018–2022 (Colorado Violent Death Reporting System)

elsewhere.text: 26% of people who died by suicide in the UK, 2013–2023, had been in contact with mental health services in the year before.
elsewhere.publisher: National Confidential Inquiry into Suicide and Safety in Mental Health, Annual Report 2026

elsewhere.text: Studies of people later diagnosed with a first psychosis find attention and memory problems often present years before.
elsewhere.publisher: Cohort research, e.g. Brewer et al., American Journal of Psychiatry, 2005

elsewhere.text: A 2024 hospital case-control study linked high-dose prescription amphetamine to 5.3 times the odds of a first psychosis or mania. It does not prove cause.
elsewhere.publisher: Moran et al., American Journal of Psychiatry, 2024

caveats: Circumstances are what investigators recorded from death certificates, coroner and police reports; categories overlap.
These describe what is written down, not a path any one person takes.
entered_from: the report's Tables 4, 5 and 6, read 20 November 2026
